title: Edge preference engine: telemetry-weighted region scoring (p50/p95) and soft failover to compatible model variants
creator: Aisha Khan
description: Build a routing component (Edge Preference Engine) that computes a single, telemetry-weighted score per region/pop using p50 and p95 latency signals plus a network health index. The score drives primary routing decisions, tier promotion/demotion, and soft failover to compatible model variants (e.g., quantized or lower-parameter family) when a region crosses degradation thresholds. Goals: maintain latency SLOs for P50/P95, minimize unnecessary model variant fallbacks, avoid thrashing between regions, and provide clear observability for decisioning. This ticket covers scoring function design, hysteresis/cooldown rules, runtime integration hooks, and rollout gating (canary + shadowing).
acceptance_criteria: Score computation implemented in the routing service and exposed via /v1/region-score endpoint (returns numeric score)
Score uses configurable weights for p50, p95, and network_health; default weights: p50=0.4, p95=0.4, net=0.2
Hysteresis: once a region is demoted/promoted, it must satisfy new score boundary for 90s before switching; cooldown window configurable
Soft failover path: automatic fallback to predefined compatible model variant with observable flag and fallback counter metric
End-to-end e2e test that simulates transient packet loss and sustained p95 spikes showing no more than one unnecessary failover in 10 minutes
Dashboards: per-region score, contributing metrics (p50/p95/net), and recent decisions; alerts on >10% traffic unexpectedly routed to fallback variant
Documentation: design doc + rollout runbook linked and PR landed for runtime config UI
notes: We intentionally avoid a strict p95-only gate because p95 noise in small POPs causes oscillation. Using a blended score with hysteresis reduced flapping in the prototype (see experiment logs). Quantized variants should be considered last-resort due to potential quality regressions; include a quality-regression monitor tied to known eval prompts.
tradeoffs: Aggressive failover reduces user latency but increases risk of quality regressions and hidden costs (larger models fallback to smaller ones may diverge outputs)
Long cooldown reduces flapping but increases MTTR for a genuinely degraded region
Simpler linear scoring is easier to operate; non-linear (exponential on p95) better isolates tail spikes but requires more tuning

release_notes_blurb: Introduce Edge Preference Engine: telemetry-weighted region scoring with configurable hysteresis and soft model-variant failovers to improve latency SLOs while reducing unnecessary fallbacks.
remediation_plan: If a rollout causes excessive quality regressions, immediately flip fallback-enabled=false via runtime feature flag and revert traffic allocations; collect failing prompts and pause the canary.
